text:
Maria Chen: seeing increased tail latency in the shared GPU pool this morning, mostly in us-west-2. head latencies are fine but 95/99th blow up.
Maria Chen: Metrics look like many tenants with small steady qps are saturating the global batching window and causing long queuing for bigger requests.
Maria Chen: example: tenant-a (commit 2 GPUs) is sending 20 small requests/sec each causing 2-3ms extra queueing per request but combined they starve tenant-b's larger inferences.
Tian Zhao: can you paste the dashboard snapshot? is it per-instance or across the pool?
Maria Chen: attached snippet from /dash/gpu-pool/us-west-2 (hover -> 10m window):
```
pool_util: 92%
avg_batch_size: 5
queue_depth: baseline 12 -> spikes 140
per_tenant_qps_top10: [tenant-a: 120, tenant-c: 85, tenant-b: 60]
95p_latency: 480ms
```
Maria Chen: looks like queue_depth correlates with a few tenants doing steady high qps with tiny seq_len.
Alex Gomez: this reads like head-of-line blocking in the single shared queue. Options: per-tenant queue shards, dynamic token-weighted rate limit, or admission control that de-prioritizes tiny requests when pool is near capacity.
Rachel K.: per-tenant queue shards would require more memory for KV caches and could increase total allocation; tough for tight clusters.
Tian Zhao: agree. I think we should try a capacity-aware admission control first: compute available GPU slots and apply soft rate caps per tenant based on their commit (or historical priority). That avoids extra state sharding.
Maria Chen: proposal draft:
```
admission_policy:
  mode: capacity_aware
  pool_threshold: 0.85  # start applying when pool_util > 85%
  tenant_cap: min( tenant_commit_gpus * 25 qps, tenant_recent_95qps * 1.5 )
  burst_window: 30s
  preemptible_buckets: 10% of pool for preemptible_short_jobs
```
Maria Chen: tenants above tenant_cap get soft-delays (HTTP 429 with Retry-After) and enter a short exponential backoff; preemptible_small_jobs can still run in reserved bucket.
Alex Gomez: I like exponential backoff + 429 approach. Keeps API semantics familiar. But risk: client SDKs might aggressively retry; we need guidance.
Rachel K.: add a header `X-Redwood-Quota-Info` with current cap, retry-after and remaining tokens. SDK can surface that.
Tian Zhao: also add a feedback loop to adjust tenant_cap using observed success rate and latency. Example: if tenant's 95p latency > 300ms and pool_util > 90% then reduce tenant_cap by 20%.
Maria Chen: good. For noisy-neighbor detection: flag tenants with high qps/low seq_len variance > threshold and mark as 'noisy' for 1h to apply stricter caps.
Alex Gomez: we should simulate with the loadgen. I'll run a synthetic run: 2000 small requests/s across 50 tenants vs baseline and test policy delta.
ops-bot: deploy queued: canary admission-policy v0.1 -> eng-sre/canary (initiated by Alex Gomez)
Alex Gomez: starting canary in us-west-2 with 2 GPUs, will run for 15m then expand to 20% of pool.
Tian Zhao: please capture these metrics during canary: pool_util, avg_batch_size, queue_depth, per_tenant_95p
Maria Chen: also track impact on CPU and KV cache miss rate since delays might cause longer KV retention.
Rachel K.: doc note: update SDK retry guidelines and add example for handling 429 with Retry-After and `X-Redwood-Quota-Info`.
Alex Gomez: action items:
- Alex: run canary load tests + collect metrics (ETD 1h)
- Tian: add adaptive reduction rule to policy (ETD 2d)
- Maria: add noisy-tenant detection heuristics and alerting (ETD 3d)
- Rachel: draft SDK guidance and header spec (ETD 2d)
Maria Chen: if canary looks good we'll roll to other regions with tweaks for region capacity and typical seq_len distributions.
Tian Zhao: one more caveat: region cross-tenant routing could send traffic to underutilized regions; ensure the admission control integrates with smart routing to avoid oscillation.
Alex Gomez: noted. will add smoothing and hysteresis to avoid back-and-forth migration.
Maria Chen: thanks team — will post canary results in this thread. :thumbsup:
